speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms better, could you tell me exactly how long you've been experiencing this bladder discomfort and frequent urination? Also, have you noticed any blood in your urine or pain during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any burning sensation or pain specifically at the start of urination, and have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle or post-menopausal status? Additionally, have you had any recent urinary tract infections or sexually transmitted infections?

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying. Do you have a history of interstitial cystitis or endometriosis, and have you noticed any pain or swelling in your pelvic area unrelated to your bladder symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Significant for bipolar disorder, currently managed with lithium. Social history: Married and sexually active with her husband. No significant alcohol, tobacco, or recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of lithium use, have you experienced excessive thirst or a significant increase in your total daily urine volume? I would also like to rule out infection, so REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the urinalysis is normal and lithium is a known cause of nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, have you noticed an excessive increase in total daily urine volume, particularly more than 3 liters per day? I will also REQUEST TEST: 24-Hour_Urine_Collection to quantify your total urine output.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your urine output and urinalysis are normal, this makes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus unlikely despite your lithium use. Given your chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding and painful intercourse, could you describe the specific nature of the pain in your lower abdomen or pelvis, and does it worsen as your bladder fills?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, hematuria, back pain, pelvic pain other than with intercourse, and any recent infections.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, frequency, and dyspareunia with negative infectious workup, this presentation is classic for Interstitial Cystitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis
